auroc_table.fl_protocol: MLP, all features, ~7.7 rounds avg, federated mean aggregation
auroc_table.manuscript_role: SUPERSEDED — different model class and feature set
auroc_table.note: Higher AUROC attributable to MLP expressivity and early-stopping on full feature set. Replaced by Phase 6 logistic-regression benchmark for adversarial analysis where computational tractability is required.

auroc_table.cohort_split: Same 2,520 stays; 80/20 stratified split fixed at seed=7
auroc_table.fl_protocol: Top-60 MI features, 15 rounds, 5 defenses x 5 seeds, adversarial benchmark
auroc_table.note: LR chosen for adversarial benchmark because: (a) tractable for 1,100 configurations x 15 rounds, (b) logistic regression is the client model in Phases 3-5, ensuring consistency. AUROC gap vs MLP (0.932 - 0.885 ~ 4.7pp) is expected from model class difference alone.

reconstruction_cosine_table.model: MLP, all features, gradient inversion, no noise
reconstruction_cosine_table.note: MLP has hundreds of parameters; gradient encodes more information per sample — reconstruction is easier.

LR gradient is a single outer-product of residuals and features divided by batch size; with 61 parameters reconstruction is ill-conditioned. Lower cosine is expected and conservative (less leakage risk than MLP baseline).

verdict: The two AUROC values (0.932 and 0.881-0.885) must not appear in the same table without attribution. Manuscript treatment: report the MLP result as a prior-work baseline in the related results section; Phase 6 LR result is the authoritative adversarial security benchmark. Add footnote: 'Centralized MLP achieves 0.932 AUROC (prior evaluation, all features); the FL logistic-regression adversarial benchmark reports 0.881-0.885 AUROC, consistent with the client model used in Phases 3-5.'
